title: A matrix node draws a grid of cells addressed by row and column
body:
`row` draws one line of cells. A two-dimensional grid of cells is one `row` per line, or one `box` per cell.

The cloud-search figure has five zoomed grids of the DP matrix, each 12 columns by 13 rows, with column numbers along the top and row numbers down the left. `gen_cloud.py` wrote each grid as 156 `box` nodes and 25 `text` nodes. Cells differ in fill, a tint for the anti-diagonal's memory slot. They differ in text, a score. And they differ in outline, a dashed red edge on a cell the search cut. One cell has a heavy outline, which took a separate `box` at hand-worked pixels.

## Proposal

A `matrix` node takes `rows`, `columns` and a cell size. It draws optional numbers along the top and the left, each with a first number and a step. Cells take text and styles by position, as `cell R C { ... }` children or from a data file. A `line`, an `arrow` or a `brace` addresses a cell as `NAME R C`, the way it addresses `ROW N` today.

## Open

- Every grid in the figure picked cells by anti-diagonal, where row + column is one number. A selector for those cells would have saved listing each one. It is less general than the node itself and can wait.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
